summary: Holopad minigames (Pazaak, Sabacc, Hintaro, Dejarik) with a world-setting session store and optional credit wagers. A-10 check: every wager debit, payout and refund goes through TransactionEngine.executeCreditAdjustment; there is no parallel credit ledger. Multi-seat atomicity is a compensating saga: per-seat debits with refund of applied debits on failure, and rollback of applied payouts. It is not one transaction, and escrow state is persisted only after all debits. Holonet's multiplayer invite path writes a wagerProfile mode ('credit-buy-in') that the escrow service does not recognize, so PvP wagers are never escrowed or paid. This fails closed: no credits move. Player-pool cashouts have no sum-to-pot conservation check at the escrow boundary. Minigame rules are not SWSE mechanics, so no rules register entries apply.

findings.title: Holonet invites use wagerProfile.mode 'credit-buy-in', which escrow does not recognize, so PvP wagers are never escrowed
findings.observed: getCreditProfile enables wagers only for modes credits/credit/buy-in/pending. The Holonet invite writes 'credit-buy-in', so isCreditWager is false. The materializer never calls prepareEscrow, and only the solo-AI engine paths call it. A wagered PvP invite therefore moves no credits and pays nothing. It fails closed, but the buy-in is shown to players. The invite path also does not apply the allowWagers/allowCreditWagers/maxCreditWager settings that the solo paths enforce.
findings.intendedOwnership: Games owns wager vocabulary and escrow; Holonet should call a games API to create sessions.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner confirms PvP credit wagers are wanted. Then have Holonet call a games-owned createInviteSession() that builds the wager profile via GameCreditEscrowService.buildCreditWagerProfile and applies the settings, and call prepareEscrow at acceptance.
findings.alternatives: Disable the buy-in field in invites until supported.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test: an invite with a buy-in produces isCreditWager === true and escrow at accept.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Two players accept a wagered Pazaak invite; credits escrow and settle.

findings.title: Wager atomicity is a compensating saga, not one transaction
findings.observed: Buy-ins are debited seat by seat. A failure refunds already-applied debits and records refund-failed evidence. Table cashouts pay seat by seat and roll back on failure. The escrow record is written only after the loop, so a reload or crash mid-loop leaves debits without an escrow record (recoverable only from TransactionEngine audit entries carrying the escrowId). Failure handling is careful and tested (G22), but this is not the 'whole trade fails' atomicity OSI asks for.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides whether compensating sagas satisfy 'atomic where possible'. If not, add a TransactionEngine multi-actor adjustment (all deltas validated, applied and verified as one operation), shared with Holonet payouts (F-HOL-002). At minimum, persist an 'escrowing' state with the escrowId before the first debit.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Reload the GM client during escrow; inspect the ledger.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One multi-party credit primitive across Holonet and games.

findings.title: No sum-to-pot conservation check for player-pool cashouts
findings.observed: settleTableCreditBalances pays each seat its engine-reported tableCredits. For player-pool sessions the policy returns approvedPayout = requested (pvpClosedLoop) and records caps.humanPool without enforcing it. Conservation therefore depends entirely on the game engines keeping total table credits equal to the pot. Not traced whether every engine guarantees this.
findings.intendedOwnership: Escrow boundary should enforce sum(payouts) <= pot for closed-loop pools.
findings.proposedSolution: Add an escrow-level invariant check that refuses or routes to GM approval when the sum exceeds the pot. Instrument it first to confirm whether it is ever violated.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test with balances exceeding the pot.

findings.title: Settlement idempotency depends on the caller's session snapshot
findings.observed: settleSession checks escrow status on the session object passed in, pays, and only then persists 'settled'. TransactionEngine's per-actor in-flight lock covers only overlapping calls. A second settle using a stale snapshot after the first payout but before persistence would pay again. Pazaak has two settle call sites (completion and forfeit).
findings.proposedSolution: Re-read the session from GameSessionStore and persist a 'settling' claim before paying (the same pattern as the Party Fund V-P6C-20 settling claim).

findings.title: Mutual games<->holonet dependency; Holonet is a second session creator
findings.observed: Holonet imports GameSessionStore and GameSessionMaterializer and writes sessions directly. Games import Holonet notification services (8 edges vs 12).
findings.intendedOwnership: Games owns sessions; Holonet owns messaging.
findings.proposedSolution: Expose one games-owned invite API (see F-GAM-001) and have games emit hooks that Holonet listens to instead of importing it.

findings.title: All game sessions in one world-setting array rewritten on every move
findings.observed: Each move rewrites and broadcasts the full sessions array (including game state and logs capped at 100), with no write serialization in the store.
findings.proposedSolution: Hypothesis: measure payload size. Add a write queue (as HolonetStorage does) and prune finished sessions.
